children: KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Genting plans to raise about 1.25 billion ringgit, equivalent to $305.9 million, through a renounceable rights issue to repay loans and fund working capital.

The company said in a bourse filing late Friday that it intends to allocate 800 million ringgit to repay borrowings, 429.5 million ringgit for working capital and 20.5 million ringgit to cover expenses related to the fundraising.

Genting expects the debt repayment to generate potential interest savings of about 41.3 million ringgit annually, based on the company's weighted average interest rate of 5.16% for short-term borrowings as of June 30.

The proposed rights issue will be offered to existing shareholders on a pro-rata basis. The issue price is expected to be set at a discount of 25% to 30% to the theoretical ex-rights price, based on the five-day volume-weighted average share price before the pricing date.

Three shareholders, namely Kien Huat Realty, Kien Huat International and Indera Lim Keong Hui have given undertakings to subscribe for their full entitlements. Based on their shareholdings as of Oct. 6, their subscriptions would total about 563.8 million ringgit, equivalent to 45.1% of the intended proceeds.
Genting expects to arrange underwriting for the remaining portion.
The fundraising comes as Genting's financial position has come under pressure.
Genting's revenue rose 8.4% on year to 14.41 billion ringgit in the first half of 2026, but net profit declined to 74 million ringgit from 248.1 million ringgit a year earlier.
Total debt, including lease liabilities, stood at 47.5 billion ringgit at the end of June, with gearing at 0.51 times.
The rights issue is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals and is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.
